answer: Randomized Task Ledge Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function (seeded by a future block hash no one controls yet) allocates incoming tasks to agents and places a random knoll: a small set of tasks whose assignment is only revealed after agents commit. An attacker cannot precompute which of their identities will be selected, so padding with cheap identities yields no advantage. To reliably capture assignments, they must maintain real capacity on every identity, paying full compute and memory per identity with no safe haven for free riders.
